title: SREV-138 ALPC local header contract

local_abi_header.description: alpc.h projects native LPC/ALPC message and port ABI shapes into Sandboxie

mirror_header.description: Sandboxie/common/win32_ntddk.h mirrors the same ALPC constants and structures

message_carrier.description: PORT_MESSAGE is the local carrier header for LPC/ALPC request, reply, and endpoint-policy payloads

private_shape_gate.description: ALPC attribute/view fields are private ABI projections and require Windows runtime capture before mutation

runtime_matrix.description: Windows LPC/ALPC service, proxy, and endpoint-policy runtime proof

shared_capture_playbook.description: Shared SREV-015/SREV-138 playbook and schema define runtime evidence records before ALPC ABI or flag mutation

contracts: alpc.h is a local ABI header and not the authoritative Windows ALPC schema
The ALPC attribute and message-view block is private-research-derived and must not be silently treated as an official Microsoft DDI
Sandboxie/core/drv/alpc.h and Sandboxie/common/win32_ntddk.h must keep shared ALPC constants and structure field names in sync
PORT_MESSAGE remains the local carrier header for Sandboxie LPC and ALPC message parsing
MAX_PORTMSG_LENGTH remains 328 because service driver and wire structs allocate fixed buffers around that value
Endpoint policy may read payload bytes only after validating the PORT_MESSAGE header and relevant DataLength TotalLength or offset range
Changes to ALPC_MESSAGE_VIEW or ALPC flags require Windows runtime capture because source-level checking cannot prove the private ABI shape
runtime capture must prove the local header mirror still matches private LPC/ALPC shapes across DLL service and driver boundaries before ABI mutation
SREV-015 and SREV-138 share docs/plan/srev-015-138-alpc-runtime-capture.schema.json as the machine-readable Windows evidence shape

negative_controls: DataLength plus PORT_MESSAGE header beyond TotalLength
unknown ALPC_MESSAGE_VIEW flags outside the accepted mask
SQOS impersonation settings that do not permit proxy behavior
